newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint closes weaker v dlr, heavy BCE futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Forint closes weaker v dlr, heavy BCE futures trade.

text.p: A combination of dollar-buying and a strong dollar/mark caused Hungary's forint to close weaker against the dollar on Tuesday, dealers said.
The forint finished some 20 pips below the central bank's resistance level (bid) at 157.38/43 to one dollar, compared to 156.90/95 at the opening.
The National Bank of Hungary's bid stood at 157.20 to the dollar at the close.
"There was some buying of dollars by Hungarian banks, which contributed to the Hungarian unit's fall," said Gabor Liener of
Unicbank. "At one point it fell to 157.40/45 but rallied a little at the end."

The forex futures market of the Budapest Commodity Exchange saw bumper trade of over 11 billion forints. Traders attributed the high turnover to recent large movements on the international forex spot markets.
The Swiss franc, which fell on Tuesday's international spot markets, dominated trade and dropped for most termins.
The mark and dollar firmed for most contracts, while the Ecu fell and the yen was mixed.
